content:
I think that file#Mathlib/SetTheory/Ordinal/Notation is in somewhat of a sorry state. It hasn't really seen any changes since @Mario Carneiro wrote it 8 years ago, and it shows. The proofs and the definitions for the arithmetic operations are all quite longer than they need to be. And it seems like every time I try and refactor anything about ordinals, that file is the first to break.

I actually did a complete rewrite about a year ago. Copying from the docstring, here's some of the changes I made:

  • The Preorder instance is no longer defined in terms of repr, thus making it computable.

  • The definition of opow is heavily simplified, avoiding multiple auxiliary definitions and
    instead relying only on natOpow.

  • Most proofs are golfed substantially by relying on new lemmas for ordinal arithmetic (in
    particular, I got rid of the long simp only chains).

I intended to PR this to Mathlib, but never got around to it. I couldn't find any natural way to split all of the changes I did, and maintainers are scant around this part of Mathlib anyways.

Recently I came up with another idea. Why not just upstream this to the CGT repository? That way, we could re-use this same type in order to implement computable natural and nimber arithmetic, both of which are of interest to CGT.

cc. @Miyahara Kō who has an open PR (#27187) duplicating some of the work I've already done.
cc. @Aaron Liu who also maintains the CGT repo.
